messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — detected routing.fallback.loop alert for route /v1/generate. Multiple hosts in eu-west-1 are returning 5xx and automated fallback is repeatedly routing traffic back and forth. Escalation: page.

amanda: Oncall Amanda here, picking this up. I'm seeing a spike in 5xx from eu-west-1 and repeated fallback events in the routing logs. Starting triage. @raj can you confirm if any manual routing overrides happened recently?

raj: I pulled the change history. There was a manual hotpatch at 2026-03-15T08:12:04Z applied by service account `eng-hotpatch` that set a sticky fallback policy for the generate route. Snippet from the policy record: 
```json
{"fallback": {"mode":"sticky","sticky_duration_secs":7200,"variant":"gpt-3.1-small-quant"}}
```
It looks like traffic got pinned to a variant in eu-west-1 that hasn't had KV-cache warmed, causing higher latency and increased error rates.

leo: Sticky fallback + region fallback is a bad combo when the variant requires per-worker warmup. Once fallback sent traffic there, sticky kept sending requests and we fed a feedback loop. Need to remove sticky ASAP so routing can round-robin between healthy variants.

maria: Quick impact numbers from the metrics dashboard: p95 latency for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.4s in the last 8m. Error rate (5xx) for that route ~12% of requests, overall region traffic saw ~18% of requests affected. We have ~6 open support tickets referencing timeouts (TKT-4321, TKT-4328).

amanda: Triage plan: 1) revert sticky fallback, 2) unpin the model variant if pinned, 3) revert any routing hotpatch that forced region-only traffic. I'll run the revert commands and watch metrics.

amanda: Running: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --route "/v1/generate" --fallback-mode round_robin
redwoodctl model unpin --route "/v1/generate" || true
```
(also posting to change control: change-id 4392)

deploy-bot: rollback/change queued: id=4392 by amanda (awaiting deployment window = immediate).

raj: Quick note — original sticky was added as an emergency mitigation to reduce downstream timeouts, but it wasn't drained and the variant didn't have warmed caches. When you unpin, consider setting a conservative `max_conns_per_host` and enable gradual shift to avoid a flash rebalance. Example: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --route "/v1/generate" --set max_conns_per_host=200 --drain-seconds=60
```

amanda: Executed revert commands at 08:18:11Z — API returned 200 OK for fallback update and unpin. Logs: `success: fallback mode set to round_robin; model unpinned`

amanda: Monitoring now — streaming metrics. 5xx started trending down within 90s of revert. p95 dropping to ~520ms, error rate down to ~6%.

pagerbot: routing.fallback.loop alert cleared for /v1/generate at 08:19:50Z. Note: some 5xx alerts remain elevated; follow-up required.

maria: Customer comms: Drafted status message for support and status.redwood.com: "We observed elevated errors and latency in EU (eu-west-1) affecting requests to /v1/generate. We applied a routing configuration rollback which has reduced errors; mitigation in progress. Root cause under investigation." Linking support tickets.

leo: Handoff/timeboxed next steps: I'll own verification and postmortem. Amanda, can you capture who applied the original sticky and the exact timeline in the incident tracker (ENG-INC-2026-2081)? Also we should add an automated guard to block sticky fallbacks without 2 approvals.

raj: FYI the change audit shows `eng-hotpatch` svc account applied the sticky at 2026-03-15T08:12:04Z and the revert at 2026-03-15T08:18:11Z by amanda. I will open a follow-up ticket to add an automated lint that prevents `fallback.mode=sticky` on regional fallbacks unless an override flag is set.

amanda: Opening PR and incident ticket now. PR will add a preflight check and a small UI/CLI confirmation for sticky fallbacks.

oncall-bot: Handoff acknowledged — primary owner leo, secondary raj. Severity set to Sev2. Keep updates in this thread; escalate to Sev1 if customer impact increases.

amanda: Thanks everyone. I'll stay on until metrics are stable. Planning to close the page in 30m if no regressions. :thumbsup:

leo: We'll include the hotpatch process and the lack of drain/warmup in the postmortem and recommend: 1) require warmup for variants before sticky handing, 2) add guarded approvals, 3) add runtime check to prevent sticky on cross-region fallbacks.

amanda: Recording timeline and notes in ENG-INC-2026-2081. Will attach logs and the policy snippet.

raj: Adding regression test to the routing simulator to reproduce sticky + fallback loops. Assigning to eng-runtime.

maria: Noted for customer follow-ups. Support will reach out to affected customers and provide timeline once postmortem is ready.

amanda: Page closed at 08:48:10Z (metrics stable). Follow-up owner: leo for postmortem. Thanks all.
